concrete_next_policy.version: CompletionBatonOwner v1, new modules only; not yet implemented as a live adapter
concrete_next_policy.initialization: Reuse frozen005 parking and first supply byte-for-byte. All22 identities remain. No substitution occurs before the first actual destination UNLOAD, subsequent HOLD/available empty state and complete received-action barrier.
concrete_next_policy.grant: A source-owned typed terminal receipt, exact business/tray/destination identity, plus current local same-tray empty stationary available state licenses one following operation. Consume the local receipt and action watermark before submit. No second owner receives the same local destination authority.
concrete_next_policy.direct_selection: Compute the frozen bridge policy's eligible peer FIFO head FIRST, using real latest delivered complete contracts and original priority. Keep that head exactly. Among the completed carrier and other current own empty carriers from the original inventory, filter actual ownership, stationary/available/no-reception/no-load, source allow/min-stock, opposite-zone target and positive mandatory paths. Rank donor alternatives by the same static public travel/service lower estimate, deterministic tray-ID tie. Select another tray only on strict improvement of that estimate; an equal estimate keeps the incumbent carrier.
concrete_next_policy.substitution: The just-completed tray remains ordinary local idle inventory. Only the chosen donor moves. No second live service is admitted before that donor's exact actual job completes and becomes available, or the declared finite attempt fails/ends unknown.
concrete_next_policy.bridge: If the frozen same-head selection needs its existing bridge fallback, bridge ONLY the just-completed tray, not an arbitrary donor. A peer grant requires a delivered native completion fact naming that tray, complete actual received-action coverage, and that exact tray currently empty at a nonloader/nonStorage local node. Its latest delivered own selfcopy must match current tray identity/node/generation/public traversal/available time and cover all its local completions. A newer local completion takes precedence; reject an old peer completion as a bridge grant if any intervening local completion exists on that tray. A pending or unknown local capture is not absence of such a completion. It may make one direct supply using the arrived tray; no bridge chain or second delegation is permitted.
concrete_next_policy.remote_identity: The peer never decodes tray/destination from opaque physical-action IDs. Direct donor identity is established by actual destination completion, not assumed from source selection. For the only empty bridge, the predeclared cooperative rule fixes it to the tray in the delivered completion receipt and actual local possession verifies it. This is a cooperative-policy invariant, not native authentication of remote payload.
concrete_next_policy.local_memory: Each owner retains consumed receipt IDs/jobs, consumed action watermark, pending immutable request, current grant phase, one-bridge flag and terminal failures. The Python ReferenceBaton uses global state solely as a test oracle; it must not be installed as an online shared global coordinator.

concrete_next_policy.native_revalidation: Use original submit_protocol_transfer/ProtocolClient retry transport,2s wire,original expiry,source load-before-export priority,min-stock,opposite-zone allow gates,receiving occupancy/reservation,edge capacity/FIFO/shield and received ACK. concrete_next_policy.faults: Pending or dropped ACK keeps the same immutable request and consumed grant; it does not grant another carrier. assumptions: Exactly the pinned original1x input and fixed positive-capacity graph/mandatory stages.
No job with an unreachable mandatory stage is ever loaded.
At every loader actual loading forms the original released FIFO prefix; this input has no same-origin equal-arrival ties.
No initial loaded jobs, bypass, job discard, off-carrier release, added source, carrier injection or goal changes.
conditional_39_lemma.proof: At each origin, loading any job after its first unreachable FIFO head requires loading that head first, contradicting the no-unreachable-load assumption. Therefore only the prefix before that head can load/complete. The sum of those11 prefix lengths is39 independently of how many existing trays are concurrently active. More trays may still complete those39 sooner. This is not a universal airport or all-contract impossibility bound.
conditional_39_lemma.371: The separate21-bad-carrier knapsack bound371 drops node/edge/FIFO-resource timing/return feasibility. It does not construct a schedule, authorize sacrificing jobs, or supersede normal protection.

beyond39_separate_feasibility.question: Could at most k of the existing22 carriers retain unreachable heads while at least one carrier continues, without bypass/discard/goal edits and while protecting the incumbent39? This is source feasibility only, not a requested native experiment.
beyond39_separate_feasibility.new_static_facts: All11 first unreachable heads require Storage53. Their absolute storage releases are19500..22200 and minimum dwell0. Crossing one bad head exposes at most15 next reachable jobs at loader24 (other nonzero gains26:1,57:4,92:1,95:2); every one of these23 additional reachable jobs ALSO requires Storage53. There is no direct-job escape in this first-bad frontier.
beyond39_separate_feasibility.native_obstruction: Storage release creates the destination storage_out leg at53. Accepted026 shield rejects a candidate without a positive-capacity suffix to the job's actual destination. Each first bad destination is unreachable from53. While such a leg remains the selected FIFO head in normal execution, it cannot physically exit under this static contract and later queued work cannot bypass it. More free trays or spare berths do not provide a legal suffix; four bad stored carriers can also consume all four Storage berths. Loaded recovery explicitly cannot release that carrier.
beyond39_separate_feasibility.existing_operation_audit: The accepted026 protocol command allowlist has route, demand/service/planning publications, forecast withdrawal and cancel_transfer. There is no job cancellation, destination replacement or loaded-job postponement command. cancel_transfer applies only to an undelivered/pending empty-transfer intent and rejects committed transfer state. Original jobs have allow_suffix_reroute=false; even an authorized preference retains the active stage goal and rejects a missing positive-capacity suffix. Storage-ready time is scheduled as max(arrival, immutable release, arrival+minimum-dwell), not a caller rescheduling request. Withholding empty supply before loading is legal admission control; after loading it is not a job cancellation or Storage-head removal mechanism.
beyond39_separate_feasibility.failure_semantics_exception: Do not claim unconditional permanent queue membership. In accepted026 try_dispatch_one, decision_count>=max_decisions_per_bag calls fail_bag and erases the chosen queue entry. Finalization also fails unfinished legs. circulation_leg_failed retains the loaded job/carrier and sets quarantine; it does not create a completed business or an empty tray. A natural same-rule failure may change later queue eligibility, subject to the remaining physical occupied berth. Deliberately exhausting a guard to discard a protected obligation is not an admitted throughput fix. Any future study must retain the unchanged failure rule, every failed job and loaded resource residual, all28506 denominator and baseline comparison.
beyond39_separate_feasibility.past_completion_protection: Waiting until all incumbent39 are actually completed would protect those past completion times by causality, if the prefix were identical. It does not solve later throughput: a newly admitted bad head still enters the same obligatory Storage as the newly exposed good jobs.
beyond39_separate_feasibility.not_proved_impossible: The present audit does not exclude all possible release/arrival orders or multipath overtaking before the bad storage_out head is queued. Such a schedule would need an exact lawful witness and protected-future proof; none is supplied. In particular, a future release time can change Storage source-queue insertion order, so merely entering Storage first is not universally the same as being its outgoing FIFO head first.
beyond39_separate_feasibility.recommended_gate: Do not start a sacrificial-carrier whole-day run from the371 number. First prove, using only currently delivered contracts and unchanged native admission, either that an exposed reachable job can complete before the bad job becomes the shared outgoing FIFO head, or that an actually natural same-rule failure dequeues it while leaving sufficient physical capacity. Retain exact observed arrival/release/queue/EDGE_ENTER/UNLOAD/HOLD/failed/quarantine/occupancy facts. Reject any purported direct repair unless its actual accepted command preserves original obligations. A future finite source-bound gate should start from a real published sealed state or reproducible original prefix, compare identical unchanged baseline/failure rules, and stop unknown if no legal witness occurs. No command or execution is prepared here; protected future completion times remain an independent requirement.
